buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 50% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 50 percent at the time of issue of the contract. However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 50 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 50 percent with the consent of the service provider 2. Provisions for workmen compensation, insurance, public liability, property damage, insurance etc. to be ensured by the contractor. Also, safety measures prescribed for working in Extra High Voltage & use of personnel protective equipment must be adhered to. 3. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses SCOPE OF WORK: Item No. 1 Assisting in Testing of 400KV SWYD CT/CVT/LA: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for the bushings/insulators as well as t hat of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs by opening nut b olts etc, assisting during the testing such as changing connection, noting readings, opening closin g isolators/breakers etc, transporting the kits / tools / cables / accessories back to the lab/store aft er testing. Item No. 2 Assisting in Testing of 400KV SWYD Circuit Breaker: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for the bushings/insulators as well as t hat of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs by opening nut b olts etc, assisting during the testing, transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the stor e/Lab after testing. Item No. 3 Assisting in Thermal scanning: Work includes transportation of Thermal scanning camera /cables/accessories from store/Lab to te st site and then assisting in completing the work by carrying thermal scanning camera around the equipment (400 kV Bay, Bus, GT and SAT, IPBD/SPBD, Generator, 6.6 kV/415V Bus duct feeder panels, motors) and assist in investigating the hot spots in all three phases, noting down the same , transporting the thermal scanning camera /cables/accessories back to the store/Lab after testing. Item No. 4 Assisting in testing of Generator transformer/Excitation Transformer/SAT: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for the bushings/insulators as well as t hat of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs by opening nut b olts etc, assisting during the testing, transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the stor e/Lab after testing. Item No. 5 Assisting in testing of Generator: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for the bushings/insulators as well as t hat of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs by opening nut b olts etc., assisting during the testing, transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the stor e/Lab after testing.

Item No. 6 Assisting in Testing of Numerical/ordinary protective relay/ Transducer/Energy met er at site: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of Panels by opening nut bolts etc., dismantling of the item if required under PPCL supervision, assisting during the testing and re-installing the item, transporting the kit s/tools/cables/accessories back to the store/Lab after testing. Item No. 7 Assisting in Testing of Numerical/other protective relay/ Transducer/Energy meter a t Electrical Lab: Work includes drawing out / dismantling the item(s) from the panel/equipment, transporting the sa me to lab/store, assisting during testing by checking/cleaning/dusting of item, preparation of test kit, making connections and in assisting test activities, packing off the kits, transporting the item(s ) back to the install location and installing back the item. Item No. 8 Checking and Cleaning of GRP/SAS/PAS/HT/LT panels: Work includes opening of panel covers & doors, thorough dusting, cleaning of relays & other instal led items, checking & tightening of all terminations, bolts etc. Item No. 9 Collection of Transformer oil sample: Work involves transporting the oil collection gear to site, connecting the SS bottle to the transform er and rinsing/cleaning of bottle and collection of the samples (1/2 bottles), bringing back to lab a nd readying the sample for test. Item No. 10 Assisting in Transformer oil testing: Work includes rinsing of BDV pot/other oil sampling device, making connections of the test devices , assisting during the testing, properly discarding of the waste oil. Item No. 11 Assisting in testing of HT/LT Motors: Work involves transporting the test kits/instruments/accessories from lab to site, opening of termi nation box, making connections and assisting during carrying out the tests and transporting the te st kits/instruments/accessories back to lab. Item No. 12 Assisting in taking IR of an electrical equipment/Cable/Bus duct: Work involves transporting the test kits/instruments/accessories from lab to site, making connecti ons and assisting during carrying out the tests and transporting the test kits/instruments/accessori es back to lab. Item No. 13 Assisting in Tan-Delta testing of a transformer: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for the bushings/insulators as well as t hat of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs by opening nut b olts etc, assisting during the testing, transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the stor e/Lab after testing. Item No. 14 Assisting in Tan-Delta testing of a Bushing set: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for the bushings as well as that of kits/ secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs by opening nut bolts etc, as sisting during the testing, transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the store/Lab after testing.

Item No. 15 Laying /removing of control/communication cables of different sizes without diggi ng/refilling: Work of cable laying includes transportation of cable from store to site and then completing the ca ble laying work with tagging and dressing in the cable trays and panels. Removing of cable includ es taking out the cable from cable trays/ trenches and making a complete roll and transporting th e cable to the store /Lab Item No. 16 Installation of new energy meter/Relay/MCB/similar equipment: Work involves taking the device/test instruments/cable/accessories from store to site, making mou nting arrangement such as drilling the plate for screw, cutting/ installing plate sections/rails, fixing screws, wiring with lugs, ferruling, from panel TBs to the device, transporting back the test instru ments/remaining cable/accessories to the lab/store. Item No. 17 Checking/cleaning/dusting and Assistance in Maintenance of OWS/EWS/LVS/GPS: Work includes opening of CPU cover, thorough dusting using brush/blower, cleaning of GPS antenn a, LVS, EWS screen with soft cloth, closing the cover of CPU and normalizing the system. Item no. 18 Checking/cleaning/dusting/Shifting of lab equipments: Work includes thorough dusting of lab equipments using blower/brush, shifting of equipments as a nd when required. Item No. 19 Making the leads for testing: Banana and crocodile clamp leads, Ethernet cables Item No. 20 Assistance in calibration of lab equipments Item No. 21 Assisting in testing of LCI Trf/Aux Trf: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for both above the bushings/insulators as well as that of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs by op ening nut bolts etc. Assisting during the testing, transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the store/Lab after testing. Item No. 22 Assisting in DC fault location by DC Scout meter (Grouser): Work involves taking the device/test instruments/cable/accessories from lab/store to site, making connections, powering up the test kit, assistance during testing such as taking the portable meter to different DC circuits, opening of panel cover door by opening nut/bolts, assisting during the test ing, transporting the kits/tools/test instrument/accessories back to store/Lab after testing. Item No. 23 Assisting in DGA of Transformer Oil Work includes making connections of the test device, powering up the instrument, putting of 01 N o. oil sample into test instrument, assisting during the testing, cleaning the instrument after compl etion of test and proper discarding of the waste oil. Item no. 24 Assisting in Testing of 6.6 KV Circuit Breaker: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for the bushings/insulators as well as t hat of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, drawing out the breaker, opening of covers of J Bs/MBs by opening nut bolts etc, assisting during the testing, putting the breaker back to service p osition, transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the store/Lab after testing. Item No. 25 Assisting in measurement of Shaft Voltage/ DC Voltage of DCDBs: Work includes transportation of measurement instrument/accessories from store/Lab to test site,

measuring of shaft voltage of all running Generators, measuring of DC voltage of all DCDBs, recor ding all the readings, transporting of measurement instrument/accessories back to store/lab. Item No. 26 Assisting in HIPOT testing: Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for the bushings/insulators as well as t hat of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs by opening nut b olts etc, assisting during the testing, transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the stor e/Lab after testing. Item No. 27 Assisting in Tan Delta Testing of 400 KV Yard Equip. Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools/cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for both above the bushings/insulators as well as that of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs by op ening nut bolts etc. Assisting during the testing such as changing connection, noting readings, ope ning closing isolators/breakers etc. Transporting the kits/ tools/cables/accessories back to the store after testing. Item No. 28 Assisting in 6.6 KV Feeders CT Testing. Work includes transportation of Test kit/tools /cables/accessories from store/Lab to test site and th en assisting in completing the work by making connections for both Primary and secondary side of CT's as well as that of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/MBs b y opening nut bolts etc. Assisting during the testing such as changing connection, noting readings, opening closing breakers etc. Transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the store after testing. Item No. 29 Assisting in Misc. Work for Prot. & Testing Deptt. Work includes any kind of electrical Misc. work that includes transportation of Test kit/tools/ cable s/accessories from store/Lab to test site and then assisting in completing the work by making con nections as well as that of kits/secondary circuits, powering up the kits, opening of covers of JBs/M Bs by opening nut bolts etc. Assisting during the testing such as changing connection, noting read ings, opening closing breakers etc..Transporting the kits/tools/cables/accessories back to the store after testing. Item No. 30 Assisting in Testing & Meter Data Work, PPS-III Work includes :- taking test instruments and accessories from lab/store to site, making connection s, assisting in testing, collecting energy meter data using portable kit and sending data to sldc (dtl ), and returning equipment to lab. Item No. 31 Assisting in Prot. Office Maint. & Support- PPS-III Work includes: - continuous upkeep of technical records, maintenance data, protection system do cumentation, compliance records, and coordination related to protection system operation and m aintenance. dusting and cleaning of office assets, furniture and accessories of dgm (tech) protecti on, manager (tech) protection and testing & protection lab at PPS-III Bawana, and assisting in day- to-day activities as assigned . Item No. 32 Assisting in Numerical Relay Comm. Check - PPS-III Work includes: - checking of numerical relays of all units and auxiliaries including healthiness of co mmunication with PAS-I, PAS-II, GPS and LVS systems at PPS-III Bawana. SPECIAL TERMS & CONDITIONS:

"Note: The bidder/vendor shall quote the rates after considering EPF, ESI, Bonus, and all other applicable s tatutory obligations. The quoted rates shall be deemed to cover compliance with all statutory provisions, i ncluding those specifically included or excluded under the Special T&C.’ 1. GENERAL: 1.1 The work shall be carried out in accordance with the Detailed Scope of Work attached as Annexure-I, w hich shall form an integral part of this tender document. 1.2 The Contractor shall provide qualified manpower, supervision, tools, tackles and associated resources necessary for satisfactory execution of the work covered under Annexure-I and as directed by the Engineer -in-Charge (EIC). 1.3 The Contractor’s manpower shall execute work (Preventive / Breakdown) at one or more locations sim ultaneously, whenever required by PPCL, without any additional financial implication to PPCL. 1.4 The Contractor shall be deemed to have fully acquainted himself with the site conditions, nature of wor k, accessibility constraints, safety requirements and operational conditions before submission of the bid. 1.5 Quantities indicated are tentative and may vary depending on site conditions and shutdown availability ; however expenditure shall remain within contract value. 2. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: 2.1 The Bidder shall possess: a) Valid Electrical Contractor License. b) EPF Registration. c) ESI Registration. 2.2 The bidder should have experience of having successfully completed works of Testing, Protection and metering activities of 220 KV / 400 KV switchyard, transformers, Generators, 6.6KV / 415V switchgears, GR Ps/SAS/PAS/AC/DC panels and associated equipments in SEBs / IPGCL-PPCL / NTPC / PSUs / DTL/ PGCIL/ Re puted large Industrial organizations. 2.3 The Bidder shall submit an undertaking confirming compliance with Regulation-7 read with Schedule-II of Central Electricity Authority (Measures Relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2010 and am endments thereof. 3. DOCUMENTS TO BE SUBMITTED: (1) The following documents, issued by Government Departments, PSUs, State Utilities, SEBs or Reputed la rge Industrial organizations, shall be uploaded on GeM at the time of bidding. a) Experience Documents (PO Copy supporting compliance with Clause 2.2 above). b) Completion Certificates. (Supporting compliance with Clause 2.2 above) c) Performance Certificates. (2) Vendor shall also submit documentary proof, which shall remain valid throughout the contract period. a) Electrical Contractor License. b) EPF Registration. c) ESI Registration. (3) Signed and stamped copy of ATC, SOW and Special T&C, as a token of acceptance. Note: - Non-submission of any mandatory document may render the bid non-responsive. PPCL may seek cl arification or shortfall documents. The bidder shall submit the same within 03 days. 4. MANPOWER REQUIREMENT: 4.1 The contractor shall deploy adequate qualified and experienced manpower, including a competent Site

-in-Charge/Supervisor, for the satisfactory execution of the work. 4.2 The Site-in-Charge/Supervisor shall possess a Diploma or Degree in Electrical Engineering and have rel evant experience in power plants/substations or similar electrical installations. 4.3 The indicative minimum manpower requirement, based on past experience for execution of the work, i s as follows: • 01 No. Site-in-Charge/Supervisor (Diploma/Degree in Electrical Engineering with 1–2 years of relevant ex perience) • 01 No. Skilled Technician/Electrician (ITI qualified with minimum 5 years of relevant experience) • 04 No. Semi-Skilled Technicians 4.4 The contractor is advised to maintain manpower deployment broadly in line with the indicative require ment specified above throughout the contract period. 4.5 The contractor shall deploy additional manpower, as and when required, to attend breakdowns, emerg ency works, or to ensure uninterrupted execution of the assigned activities without any extra cost to the o wner. 4.6 PPCL may seek replacement of unsuitable manpower and the Contractor shall provide replacement wit hin 24 hours. 4.7 Contractor personnel shall remain employees of the Contractor only and shall have no claim whatsoev er against PPCL regarding employment, regularization, wages, compensation, absorption, service benefits or any other employment-related matter. PPCL shall have no employer-employee relationship with the perso nnel deployed by the Contractor. 5. MOBILIZATION & WORK EXECUTION: 5.1 Preventive maintenance work shall normally be informed up to 8 hours in advance. 5.2 For emergency/breakdown situations, contractor shall mobilize manpower within 1 hour on round‑the‑c lock basis. 5.3 Work shall start only after obtaining Permit‑to‑Work (PTW) or instruction from the Engineer‑in‑Charge. 5.4 After issuance of the Permit-to-Work (PTW) to the Contractor’s Supervisor, the Contractor shall be solel y responsible for safe execution and completion of the assigned job in compliance with all applicable rules and standards. After completion, the Supervisor shall clear the site of all manpower, tools, and materials a nd submit the Job Completion Report while requesting the PPCL Site Engineer for PTW cancellation. 5.5 After PTW cancellation/closure, the PPCL Engg. / Site Engineer may carry out trial/run-testing of the con cerned equipment/system. The Contractor/Contractor’s Supervisor shall be solely responsible for ensuring safe and successful trials and shall extend all necessary support to PPCL. 5.6 Preventive maintenance activities shall be completed within the stipulated time as intimated by the PP CL Site Engineer. 6. CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITIES: 6.1 The Contractor shall inspect site conditions before bidding. 6.2 Contractor personnel shall remain within authorized work areas only. 6.3 All incidental expenses shall be borne by the Contractor. 6.4 No additional payment, reimbursement, escalation, DA, allowance, or claim or any other charges of wh atsoever nature shall be admissible on any account, including site constraints, weather conditions, shutdo wn restrictions, travel, accommodation, transportation, logistics, statutory compliances, or any other incid ental expenses required for execution of the work. 7. DOCUMENTATION & BILLING:

7.1 Monthly bills shall be accompanied by: a) Wage Slip / Register. b) Bank Transfer Proof. c) EPF Challans. d) ESI Challans. e) Bonus Payment Proof. 7.2 Bills shall normally be submitted by the second week of the succeeding month. 7.3 The Contractor’s Supervisor shall maintain all work-related records, logs, and reports in the prescribed format as directed by the PPCL Engineer-in-Charge and submit the same as required. 8. PAYMENT TERMS: 8.1 Payment shall be released on monthly basis after certification by Engineer-in-Charge. 8.2 Payment shall normally be released within 30 days after submission of complete documents. 8.3 Wage payment shall be made by the Contractor on or before the 7th of every month through banking channels only. 8.4 No idle charges shall be payable by the department. 9. CONTRACT AGREEMENT & INDEMNITY BOND: 9.1 The successful bidder shall submit the following documents on non-judicial stamp papers in the prescri bed PPCL format before commencement of work: (a) Contract Agreement on Rs.100/- Non-Judicial Stamp Paper. (b) Indemnity Bond on Rs.10/- Non-Judicial Stamp Paper. The cost of stamp papers and execution of documents shall be borne by the Contractor. 10. CONTRACT PERIOD: 10.1 Contract Period shall be One Year from commencement of work or exhaustion of contract value, whic hever is earlier. 10.2 Extension may be considered for up to six months on mutual consent. 11. TOOLS & TACKLES: 11.1 Specialized testing equipment may be provided by PPCL wherever available. 11.2 Contractor shall arrange all general tools, tackles and consumables such as multimeter, clamp meter, spanners, screwdrivers, insulation tape, drill machine, cleaning materials etc. 11.3 Tools and consumables shall be available within 7 days of start of contract. 12. SAFETY & STATUTORY COMPLIANCE: 12.1 The Contractor shall comply with all applicable safety regulations. 12.2 The Contractor shall comply with all statutory safety requirements, safety procedures, permit conditio ns and instructions issued by PPCL from time to time. 12.3 PPE including helmets, safety shoes, gloves and safety belts shall be provided by the Contractor. 12.4 Any accident, injury, fatality, loss of life, property damage or equipment damage occurring during execution of the work shall be immediately reported to PPCL and shall remain the sole responsibility and li ability of the Contractor.

12.5 Safety of contractor personnel, tools, tackles, equipment and work execution shall be the sole respon sibility of the Contractor. 12.6 PPCL reserves the right to stop any work being carried out in an unsafe manner. No claim for idling, d elay, compensation or additional payment shall be entertained on this account. 12.7 Repeated safety violations shall be treated as a breach of contract and may attract penalties, suspen sion of work, risk & cost action, or termination of contract. 13. CONFIDENTIALITY: All technical data, relay settings, SAS/SCADA information, drawings, passwords and plant-related informati on shall remain confidential and shall not be disclosed without written approval of PPCL. 14. LABOUR LAW COMPLIANCE: (1) The Contractor shall comply with: a) Minimum Wages Act. b) EPF Act. c) ESI Act. d) Bonus Act. e) Contract Labour Act. f) Workmen Compensation Act. g) Any other applicable statutory provisions. (2) Minimum wages shall be paid as notified by Government of NCT of Delhi. (3) Wherever ESI coverage is not applicable under the relevant statutory provisions, the Contractor shall ar range and maintain a Health Insurance Policy with a minimum coverage of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lak h only) per worker/family for all personnel deployed under the contract. Documentary evidence of such ins urance shall be submitted to PPCL whenever demanded by PPCL. 15. INSURANCE & INDEMNITY: 15.1 The Contractor shall maintain: a) Workmen Compensation Insurance. b) Public Liability Insurance. c) Property Damage Insurance. Insurance policies shall be submitted before commencement of work. 15.2 Public Liability Insurance shall provide coverage for bodily injury, death or disability arising out of exe cution of the contract with minimum limits as follows: (a) Not less than Rs.1,00,000/- for any one person. (b) Not less than Rs.2,00,000/- for any one accident. 15.3 Property Damage Insurance shall provide coverage of not less than Rs.1,00,000/- for each accident. 15.4 Failure to maintain valid insurance coverage shall be treated as a material breach of contract and PP CL shall be at liberty to suspend the work until compliance is ensured. 15.5 The Contractor shall be solely responsible for any accident, injury, fatality, loss, damage, or statutory non-compliance arising during execution of the work and shall indemnify PPCL against all related claims, li abilities, penalties, costs, and legal proceedings. An undertaking to this effect shall be submitted by the Contractor before commencement of the work. 16. PENALTY & RISK PURCHASE:

16.1 Failure to mobilize manpower, attend breakdowns or execute assigned work shall invite Risk & Cost a ction. 16.2 Delay in completion of job may attract penalty up to job cost depending on severity. 16.3 Absence of supervisor/site-in‑charge may attract penalty of ₹500 per day. 16.4 Non‑availability of tools/consumables affecting work may attract penalty ₹500 per instance. 16.5 Delay in payment of wages may attract penalty up to 1% per week subject to maximum 5% of runnin g bill. 17. MISCELLANEOUS: 17.1 Contractor shall comply with Factory Act provisions, plant safety rules and statutory safety regulation s. 17.2 PPCL reserves the right to execute work through other agencies at the risk and cost of contractor in c ase of non performance. 17.3 The Contractor shall maintain a valid and functional official website throughout the contract period a nd ensure that all information displayed therein complies with applicable laws, regulations, and contractual requirements. 18. EMD may be furnished, details of which uploaded on web site, in any of the following forms. Demand Draft in favour of PPCL Bank Guarantee from a Nationalized Bank/scheduled bank irrevocable and operative till the validity of the offer as per standard Proforma. ECS may be done on https://www.onlinesbi.com/sbicollect/icollecthome.htm?corpID=8540, link available o n IPGCL-PPCL website. No BG shall be accepted for EMD amount up to Rs. 25,000/-. In the NIT, it should be clearly stipulated that the vendors should submit EMD in a separate marked envelop and not to enclose the same with any part o f the quotation. No request for adjustment of earlier dues in place of EMD shall be entertained. Note: No BG shall be accepted for EMD amount up to Rs. 25,000/-. 19. The exemption from Earnest Money deposit (EMD) shall be extended only to those MSME vendors who are registered under the Service/Manufacturer/Trader Category as Micro or Small Enterprises (MSEs) and w hose Udyam Registration covers the relevant product/activity as per tender’s scope of work. 20. INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING COMMON IP ADDRESS: Bidders are advised to note that if any bid is found to have a matching or common IP a ddress with any other bidder on the Delhi Government e-Portal, all such bids shall be o utrightly rejected without any further communication and will not be considered for fur ther evaluation. Special Note : The bidder shall quote only the percentage (+/–) above or below the total BOQ valu e. The quoted percentage shall be uniformly applicable to all activities/items of the BOQ. Any change in individual unit rates shall not be permitted and, if quoted, the bid shall be liable for outright rejection/necessary actio n. So please fill only Company/firm name and percentage (+/–) above or below tab in BOQ. .
